## Define the study

`cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration()` creates a study environment and its folders.
Pass that environment to both `getDataForStudy()` and `createTrajectories()`.
Configuration alone does not retrieve patient data or generate trajectories.

The analyst defines the target and state cohorts. The target cohort supplies
the observation interval. State cohorts supply the clinical facts to represent
within that interval. Cohort2Trajectory does not infer the meaning of a state
from its label.

This example uses cohort definitions from an ATLAS WebAPI. Replace the URL and
cohort IDs with your own. Each state ID has one label in the same position.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(Cohort2Trajectory)

studyEnv <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "example",
  pathToStudy = getwd(),
  useCDM = TRUE,
  baseUrl = "http://localhost:8080/WebAPI",
  atlasTargetCohort = 101,
  atlasStateCohorts = c(202, 203),
  stateCohortLabels = c("A", "B"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("B", "A"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  lengthOfStay = 7
)
```

Use `"Discrete"` or `"Continuous"` for `trajectoryType` and `"First"`,
`"Overlap"` or `"Priority"` for `stateSelectionType`. These options accept
names, not numeric codes. Discrete trajectories also need a positive whole
number of days for `lengthOfStay`. The
[trajectory article](a03_trajectories.html) explains selection and gap handling.

Labels must be nonempty and unique even when ignoring case. `"0"`, `"START"`,
`"EXIT"` and `"OUT OF COHORT"` are reserved. Keep the same spelling in labels,
priorities and rule-source names. Labels are not filenames.

## Choose only the rules you need

`stateCohortMandatory = NULL` and `stateCohortAbsorbing = NULL` mean no mandatory
or absorbing states. `character(0)` also means none. Do not add a placeholder
state to express the absence of a rule.

A mandatory state must occur somewhere in the patient's retained interval.
It does not mean that the patient must be in that state on Day 7 or at another
specified time. Define time-specific eligibility in the target cohort when
that is part of the study design. Mandatory requirements are applied during
import, so changing them requires another import.

An absorbing state ends a trajectory when it is retained by the selection and
transition rules. Use the exact state label in `stateCohortAbsorbing`.

By default, `allowedStatesList` permits transitions between the configured
states. Supply a named list to restrict them. An empty list imposes no
restrictions. The [function reference](../reference/cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration.html)
describes the full rule syntax.

## Merge overlapping states when needed

Set `mergeStates = TRUE` to represent exact overlaps as states with explicit
membership. For example, an overlap between `"A"` and `"B"` has both as members.
The package does not split a display label to recover those members.

Merged states inherit rules from their members. To replace selected properties,
build an override and pass it as `mergedStateOverrides` when configuring the study.
Omitted properties keep their inherited values.

The default rules are:

- If A can enter C, A+B can enter C even when B cannot.
- To enter C+D, both newly added members must be permitted by at least one
  source member. Permission for C alone is not enough.
- Staying in A+B, or moving from A+B to A, requires permission for every
  member retained at the destination. An empty destination list does not
  automatically allow a self-transition.
- If any member is absorbing, the combination is absorbing. Its priority is
  the highest priority of its members. Larger combinations come first when
  that priority is equal.

Merging uses the original dates before cycles are constructed. A on days 1 to
10 and B on days 5 to 7 produce A, then A+B, then A again. Two non-overlapping
events within the same week are not combined merely because they share a cycle.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
overrides <- list(
  mergedState(
    members = c("A", "B"),
    label = "A and B",
    allowedTransitions = "B",
    absorbing = FALSE
  )
)
```

This override requires `mergeStates = TRUE`. Its destinations and absorbing
status replace the inherited values. See the
[merged-state reference](../reference/mergedState.html) for further examples
and [output files](a05_output.html) for the state dictionary.

## Supply a CDM connection when running the study

Create a CDM reference with CDMConnector using your site's database connection
and a writable schema. For example, with an existing DBI connection named
`connection`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
cdm <- CDMConnector::cdmFromCon(
  con = connection,
  cdmSchema = "cdm",
  writeSchema = c(schema = "results", prefix = "c2t_")
)

getDataForStudy(cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(cdm = cdm, studyEnv = studyEnv)
```

The connection is supplied to these calls, not stored for reuse in saved study
settings. For a data frame or CSV instead of a CDM, set `useCDM = FALSE` and
follow the [local input example](a02_import.html#local-data).

## Repeat a saved study

After successful import and trajectory generation, the study contains
`Settings/analysisSettings.rds`. The current snapshot format is version 4.
It stores the analysis settings and, for a CDM study, the cohort JSON definitions
used during import. It does not contain patient data or a database connection.

Copy the completed study's `Settings` folder to
`new-study-location/example/Settings`. JSON and Data folders are not needed for
a saved CDM run. Connect to the new database and restore the study:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
savedStudy <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "example",
  pathToStudy = "new-study-location",
  runSavedStudy = TRUE
)

getDataForStudy(cdm = newCdm, studyEnv = savedStudy)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(cdm = newCdm, studyEnv = savedStudy)
```

Do not repeat labels, rules or cycle settings in these calls. They are restored
from the snapshot. Saved runs import fresh patients using the embedded
definitions, not edited files in the working JSON folder. To change analysis
rules or cohort definitions, configure a fresh study and complete both steps.
Older snapshot formats must also be rerun before they can be shared this way.

A saved local-data study restores its rules in the same way. Set `useCDM = FALSE`
and supply a new data frame or CSV, as described in the
[import article](a02_import.html#saved-studies).
